name: SENEGAL
lead: Senegal sits at Africa's westernmost tip. Its capital, Dakar, buzzes with music and fish stew. Giant baobab trees dot the savannah, and one lake is pink! People live by teranga, a Wolof word for warm welcome. Strangers feel like family at once.

facts.label: Capital
facts.sub: On the Atlantic tip of Africa

geo: Senegal is almost flat. Dry plains lie in the north and green forest in the south. The country wraps around tiny Gambia on three sides.
Lake Retba, north of Dakar, turns pink from tiny salt-loving plants. It is saltier than the Dead Sea. Workers harvest its salt every day.
animals: Niokolo-Koba National Park shelters some of West Africa's last wild lions, hippos and chimpanzees. It covers 9,000 km² of savannah. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Djoudj Bird Sanctuary welcomes up to 3 million birds each winter. Great white pelicans arrive in white clouds. Senegal has over 660 bird species.
culture: Music beats at the heart of Senegal. Youssou N'Dour, a singer, mixed sabar drums with jazz to make mbalax. Griots, storytellers by birth, remember centuries of history and sing it.
Guests are fed before anyone asks their name. That is teranga. Wrestling, called laamb, is as loved as football. Wrestlers dance before 70,000 fans.
history: Two old kingdoms, Ancient Ghana and Jolof, once ruled here. From the 1400s, Europeans held enslaved Africans on Gorée Island, 3 km off Dakar. The Door of No Return still stands there.
France ruled until 4 April 1960. Then Senegal became independent under poet-president Léopold Sédar Senghor. Power has passed peacefully ever since.
wows: Lake Retba is saltier than the Dead Sea, so you float easily!
Dakar's African Renaissance Monument is taller than the Statue of Liberty.
Senegal nearly wraps around Gambia on three sides, like a hug.
Top wrestlers earn more than footballers and fill stadiums of 70,000 fans.
Baobab trees can live 1,000 years and store tonnes of water.
Senegal has had no military coups since independence in 1960.
Youssou N'Dour has sold 30 million albums and served as a minister.

myths.myth: Baobab trees grow with roots in the air
myths.fact: Bare branches only look like roots in the dry season. The fruit becomes a tangy juice called bouye.

myths.myth: The Dakar Rally still ends in Dakar
myths.fact: The race began in 1978 and finished in Dakar until 2007. Today it is held in Saudi Arabia.
